Students do repeat and apply the word in their own speech via the sentence stem, which counts as use. The core steps show students using the word "setting" in structured discussion. However, the variety-of-settings requirement is only partially met — communication occurs in partner discussions and independent writing but the lesson doesn't explicitly demonstrate a variety of settings. On reflection, the standard says "in a variety of settings" but students do communicate in partner talk and whole-group share and independent writing, which constitutes some variety. Let me reconsider: students do use the vocabulary word "setting" in their own speech via sentence frames in core steps. This meets "use to communicate." The interchangeable object list means meeting any one of general/academic/specialized suffices. The word "setting" qualifies as academic vocabulary. Students use it in partner discussions and whole-group sharing — multiple settings. This should be full.
Standard text: Use grade-level general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words and phrases to communicate in a variety of settings. (C)
